Definition: of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently:--forbear, spare.
BiblicalUsage: Pheidomai means to spare, to hold back, to be chary of, and Scripture uses it both ways. Paul says God did not spare His own Son but delivered Him up for us all, and warns that if God did not spare the natural branches He will not spare us either. He tells the Ephesian elders that grievous wolves will enter in, not sparing the flock, and Peter says God did not spare the angels that sinned.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe spared and not spared is the gospel in one verb: God did not spare His Son, so that He could spare me. The same God who did not spare the angels will not spare a branch that trusts in itself, and the wolves will not spare the flock. My position is that my safety is not in being spared from trouble but in being held by the One who was not spared for me.
